articles.title: Telangana Issues Solar Tender Requiring Use Of Only TOPCon Technology
articles.description: The Telangana Renewable Energy Development Corporation Limited (TGREDCO) has issued a tender for the design, supply, installation and commissioning of a 33 kW grid-connected rooftop solar project in Karimnagar, with the procurement specifically requiring the use of TOPCon solar modules. The tender covers rooftop solar installations across five government facilities under the District Veterinary and Animal Husbandry Office (DVAHO), Karimnagar. The systems will be implemented under net metering and will include a five-year comprehensive maintenance contract (CMC). The project is divided across five locations, with a 10 kW system proposed at the Joint Director, DVAHO office, 8 kW at the Veterinary Hospital, DVAHO, and 5 kW each at three other facilities — the Veterinary Hospital, Veterinary Surgeon office and Assistant Director's office. TOPCon technology specifically mandated A key feature of the tender is the explicit requirement for TOPCon solar modules. The tender document identifies the scope as an aggregated 33 kW on-grid rooftop solar PV project “with Topcon Solar Modules” and a five-year comprehensive maintenance contract. The modules supplied under the project must be included in the MNRE Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM), as amended from time to time. They must also comply with the latest applicable IEC or equivalent BIS standards, including IEC 61215/IS 14286, IEC 61853 Part I/IS 16170 Part I, IEC 61730 Parts 1 and 2 and IEC 62804 for potential-induced degradation (PID). The tender specifies a minimum module efficiency of 20% and a minimum fill factor of 75%. The temperature coefficient of power must be equal to or better than -0.45% per degree Celsius. The modules are also required to carry a performance warranty of more than 90% during the first 10 years and more than 80% during the subsequent 15 years. Project to follow CAPEX model The tender will be executed under the CAPEX model. The successful bidder will be responsible for the complete design, supply, installation and commissioning of the grid-connected rooftop systems. The scope includes solar PV modules, inverters and remote monitoring systems, module mounting structures, energy meters, array junction boxes, DC and AC distribution boxes, earthing, lightning and surge protection, cables and associated civil works. The financial bid requires bidders to quote a price in rupees per kWp for the 33 kW installation. The quoted price is to include the five-year CMC as well as taxes, duties, transportation, installation, commissioning, connectivity charges and other associated costs. Eligibility criteria TGREDCO has stipulated that bidders must have experience of installing at least 33 kW of cumulative grid-connected rooftop solar PV systems at government buildings or under subsidy schemes in any one of the last three financial years — FY 2023-24, FY 2024-25 or FY 2025-26. Bidders using PM-Surya Ghar installations to meet the experience requirement must submit the relevant synchronization report along with the agreement signed with the consumer. The minimum financial eligibility requirement has been set at ₹22 lakh turnover in any one of the last three financial years. Valid TGREDCO vendor registration, PAN and GST registration are also mandatory. The tender was issued on August 12, 2026, with the deadline for uploading bid documents set for August 27, 2026. Why the tender stands out While the project itself is relatively small at 33 kW, the explicit specification of TOPCon technology is noteworthy. Rather than simply prescribing crystalline PV modules and efficiency parameters, TGREDCO has identified TOPCon modules in the project scope, alongside ALMM eligibility and minimum performance requirements. This makes the Karimnagar procurement a specific government rooftop solar tender where TOPCon technology is expressly built into the technical requirement. By ruling our MonoPerc, Bifacials that dominate the market, and even the thin film CdTe modules of First Solar, the requirement is bound to raise some questions on just what made the authority go with the TOPcon specification.

articles.title: MNRE Extends Rooftop Solar Phase II Subsidy Claim Deadline To Nov 30
articles.description: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) has extended the deadline for submitting claims for Central Financial Assistance (CFA) under the erstwhile Grid Connected Rooftop Solar (RTS) Phase II programme to November 30, 2026, providing additional time for eligible consumers whose rooftop solar installations have reached the redeemed, inspected or installed stage. According to the amended operational guidelines for the PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, all applications under the Phase II rooftop solar programme that have reached the redeemed, inspected or installed stage will remain eligible for CFA, provided the claim is received by November 30, 2026. The CFA for these applications will continue to be governed by the respective RTS Phase II programme guidelines. Replacing Earlier Deadline The latest amendment replaces the earlier deadline of December 31, 2025, for submission of such claims. Importantly, the amended clause removes the earlier provision dealing with applications that had been submitted under the Phase II programme but remained uninstalled as of April 1, 2025. Under the earlier provision, such applications were to be declared ineligible for CFA and deleted from the database, with consumers allowed to re-apply under PM-Surya Ghar in the future. The revised clause no longer contains this provision. The move comes as the government continues to transition legacy rooftop solar applications from the Grid Connected Rooftop Solar Phase II programme into the PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana framework. The Phase II programme, which had been implemented through both tender and National Portal modes, was subsumed into PM-Surya Ghar following the launch of the new scheme on February 13, 2024. The PM-Surya Ghar guidelines provide that ongoing liabilities under the earlier programme would continue to be met from the new scheme's budgetary outlay, while claims would be governed by the applicable Phase II guidelines. Phase II claims retain earlier subsidy structure For applications received under the Phase II programme before the launch of PM-Surya Ghar, the applicable subsidy depends on when the first claim was submitted. Claims submitted before January 5, 2024, are eligible for subsidy of ₹14,588/kW for capacity up to 3 kW and ₹7,294/kW for capacity beyond 3 kW up to 10 kW. For claims first submitted on or after January 5, 2024, the applicable rates are ₹18,000/kW for capacity up to 3 kW and ₹9,000/kW thereafter up to 10 kW. In contrast, new applications under PM-Surya Ghar are covered by the scheme's revised CFA structure, under which residential consumers receive support for up to 3 kW of rooftop solar capacity, with no additional CFA beyond 3 kW. What the November 30 deadline means The latest amendment effectively gives the remaining eligible Phase II applications additional time to complete the claim process. The key condition is that the application must have already reached the redeemed, inspected or installed stage under the Phase II programme. The amended provision does not, however, specify in the displayed clause any fresh eligibility for applications that had not reached these stages. Instead, it removes the earlier explicit provision that such uninstalled applications as of April 1, 2025 would be deleted and could subsequently re-apply under PM-Surya Ghar. For eligible legacy projects, the extension could help prevent the loss of subsidy claims because the CFA under Phase II continues to be determined according to the programme's original guidelines rather than the newer PM-Surya Ghar subsidy structure. The PM-Surya Ghar scheme itself is targeting one crore residential rooftop solar installations and is scheduled to run until March 31, 2027.

articles.title: Bengaluru meat shops may shut for two days over waste dispute
articles.description: The Karnataka Poultry Traders Association says meat shops may remain closed on August 3 and 4, with owners planning a protest at Freedom Park over the collection and commercial use of meat waste. Meat lovers in Bengaluru could face difficulty buying non-vegetarian food if meat shop owners go ahead with their proposed two-day shutdown. The Karnataka Poultry Traders Association has said that meat shops across Bengaluru may remain closed on August 3 and 4. According to the association, shop owners have decided to take this step after failing to get a favourable response to their concerns over the collection and handling of meat waste. The traders are also planning to hold a protest at Freedom Park, where they intend to raise their demands against the government. At the centre of the dispute is the system used to collect meat waste from shops across Bengaluru. According to the association, the Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Limited (BSWML) is responsible for collecting meat waste. The traders allege that BSWML has awarded a tender to private companies to collect this waste. Also Read: Bengaluru-Tumakuru Highway toll hike: Up to ₹245 more for return journey from today The association further alleges that these private companies are collecting ₹5 for every kilogram of meat waste from shop owners. The traders are questioning why they should have to pay for waste that, according to them, has commercial value. Their claim is that the collected meat waste is subsequently processed and used for different purposes. They allege that the waste is being used in products ranging from dog food, including products such as Pedigree, to manure, which is then sold. The meat shop owners argue that companies are therefore earning money from the waste generated by their businesses while also asking the traders to pay for collecting it. The association has questioned this arrangement and is demanding a change in the system. Their primary demand is straightforward: if meat waste has commercial value, the traders should be paid for the waste instead of being charged for handing it over. The traders want the authorities to introduce a system under which they receive money when their meat waste is collected. Also Read: BMTC launches new metro feeder route from KR Market to Bilekahalli The association says it has already raised the issue with the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) and Minister Krishna Byre Gowda. However, the traders claim that their representations have not resulted in any solution. With their concerns still unresolved, the association says it has decided to intensify the protest. The traders have therefore announced that they will shut their meat shops on August 3 and 4 and gather at Freedom Park to stage a protest and press for their demands. The proposed shutdown could affect customers across Bengaluru who depend on meat shops for poultry and other non-vegetarian products. For the traders, however, the issue is primarily about the way meat waste is collected and the money involved in its subsequent use. They are demanding that the waste generated by their businesses should not become an additional expense for them when it is allegedly being converted into commercially useful products.

articles.title: Harish to Revanth: It’s easy to abuse Former Telangana CM KCR, but you can’t rule like him
articles.description: T Harish Rao demanded that the chief minister immediately withdraw the remarks he made against KCR and tender an unconditional apology to the former chief minister.
